source_text: Ἑαυτῷ δὲ λαμβάνει ὡς ἡμετέραν ἀπόκρισιν πρὸς πεῦσιν αὐτοῦ λεγομένην φήσαντος· τίνι προσήχθητε λογισμῷ τοῦτον νομίζειν υἱὸν θεοῦ; πεποίηκε γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἀποκρινομένους ὅτι τούτῳ προσήχθημεν, (ἐπ) εὶ καὶ ἴσμεν τὴν κόλασιν αὐτοῦ ὑπὲρ καθαιρέσεως τοῦ πατρὸς τῆς κακίας γεγονυῖαν. ἄλλοις γὰρ μυρίοις προσήχθημεν, ὧν πολλοστημόριον ἐν τοῖς πρὸ τούτων ἐξεθέμεθα καὶ θεοῦ διδόντος ἐκθησόμεθα οὐ μόνον ἐν τοῖς πρὸς τὸν νομιζόμενον Κέλσου ἀληθῆ λόγον πραγματευόμενοι ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις μυρίοις. καὶ ὡς ἡμῶν γε λεγόντων ὅτι υἱὸν αὐτὸν νομίζομεν θεοῦ, ἐπεὶ ἐκολάσθη, φησί· τί οὖν; οὐχὶ καὶ ἄλλοι πολλοὶ ἐκολάσθησαν, καὶ οὐχ ἧττον ἀγεννῶς; ὅμοιον δ᾿ ἐν τούτῳ ποιεῖ ὁ Κέλσος τοῖς ἀνδραποδωδεστάτοις τῶν ἐχθρῶν τοῦ λόγου καὶ οἰομένοις ὅτι ἀκολουθεῖ τῇ περὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἱστορίᾳ σταυρωθέντα τὸ σέβειν ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἐσταυρωμένους.
pass_a_gloss: And he takes (λαμβάνω) for himself as our answer (ἀπόκρισις) spoken to his inquiry (πεῦσις), having said: by what reasoning (λογισμός) were you brought (προσάγω) to think (νομίζω) this one Son of God? For he has made us answering that we were brought to this, since (ἐπεί) we also know that his punishment (κόλασις) came about for the overthrow (καθαίρεσις) of the father of vice/evil (πατὴρ τῆς κακίας). For by countless (μυρίοι) other things we were brought, of which a very small part (πολλοστημόριον) we set forth (ἐκτίθημι) in the things before these, and God granting (δίδωμι) we will set forth not only treating (πραγματεύομαι) against the supposed (νομιζόμενος) true discourse (ἀληθὴς λόγος) of Celsus but also in countless others. And as if we said that we think him Son of God since he was punished, he says: what then? were not many others also punished, and not less ignobly (ἀγεννῶς)? And Celsus in this does like the most slavish (ἀνδραποδωδέστατοι) of the enemies of the doctrine/word (λόγος), and [those] thinking that it follows (ἀκολουθέω) from the history (ἱστορία) about Jesus crucified (σταυρόω) that we revere (σέβω) the crucified.
pass_b_english: He supplies for himself, as if it were our answer, a reply to a question of his own, when he says: “By what reasoning were you led to think that this man is the Son of God?” For he has represented us as answering that we were led to it because we know that his punishment took place for the overthrow of the father of wickedness. In fact we were led by countless other reasons, of which we have set out a very small part in what has gone before; and, if God grants it, we shall set them out not only in our work against Celsus’s so-called True Doctrine, but in countless other works as well.

And as though we said that we think him the Son of God because he was punished, he says: “What then? Were not many others punished too, and no less ignobly?” In this Celsus acts like the most slavish-minded of the enemies of our teaching, who think it follows from the story of Jesus crucified that we worship those who have been crucified.

choices.why: "he has made us answer" made "he has represented us as answering" (πεποίηκε ... ἀποκρινομένους)
"But we were led" made "In fact we were led" (γάρ, not a contrast)
"our treatment of what Celsus takes to be a True Doctrine" made "our work against Celsus's so-called True Doctrine" (νομιζόμενον is passive "reputed", not Celsus's own view; πρὸς = against)

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; English is from the Greek.

translator_notes: Koetschau supplies (ἐπ)εί; the text reads “because we know”. Celsus’s question and his reply (“What then? ...”) are quoted directly; the answer he puts in Christians’ mouths is reported indirectly and is not set in quotation marks. πεποίηκε ... ἡμᾶς ἀποκρινομένους is “he has represented us as answering”. “The overthrow of the father of wickedness” (πατὴρ τῆς κακίας, the devil) may echo Hebrews 2:14 or 1 John 3:8, but the wording does not match closely and the words are Celsus’s caricature, so no inline citation is given. ἄλλοις γὰρ μυρίοις is rendered “In fact we were led by countless other reasons”, keeping the explanatory γάρ. τὸν νομιζόμενον Κέλσου ἀληθῆ λόγον is rendered “Celsus’s so-called True Doctrine” (νομιζόμενον = “supposed, reputed”), keeping the title of his book; πρὸς gives “our work against”. ἐχθροὶ τοῦ λόγου could be “enemies of the Word” or “of our teaching”; “enemies of our teaching” gives the plain sense without claiming a reference to Christ as Word. ἀνδραποδωδέστατοι is rendered “most slavish-minded”. ἀγεννῶς is rendered “ignobly” (basely, without dignity).
